newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian support for peace eroding - poll.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian support for peace eroding - poll.

text.p: Israel's settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem is chipping away at Palestinian support for peace moves with the Jewish state, according to an opinion poll released on Wednesday.

The Jerusalem Media and Communications Centre poll of 1,200 Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza on April 3-4 showed 73 percent of those surveyed said they supported the peace process. A JMCC poll last month put the figure at 78 percent.
"There is a downward slope in only a period of three weeks," pollster Jamil Rabah told Reuters. "It is clear that unless there is a political breakthrough, it will snowball."
The poll was taken after Israel broke ground for 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa in Hebrew.
Opposition to the U.S.-sponsored peace process rose from 18.8 percent to 23.1 percent, the poll said.
The poll also showed that 47.7 percent of those surveyed said they oppose "military operations against Israeli targets" and 39.8 percent voiced support.
The poll said 62.7 percent of Palestinians want to step up anti-Israeli protests that have flared almost daily since work began at the East Jerusalem site.
